title: The Fragility of Strategic Thinking in Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2510.10813v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to domains that require reasoning about other agents' behavior, such as negotiation, policy design, and market simulation. However, can we trust LLMs to think strategically in complex situations? Existing research mostly evaluates LLMs' adherence to equilibrium play or their exhibited depth of reasoning, leaving open whether they display strategic thinking meant as the ability to form coherent conjectures about other agents, to evaluate possible actions conditional on those conjectures, and to best respond to them. We develop a framework to identify this ability by disentangling belief formation, evaluation, and choice in static complete-information games across a series of non-cooperative environments. translated_title: 大型语言模型中战略思维的脆弱性
translated_abstract: arXiv:2510.10813v2 公告类型：替换 摘要：大型语言模型（LLMs）越来越多地被应用于需要推理其他智能体行为的领域，例如谈判、政策设计和市场模拟。然而，我们能否信任LLMs在复杂情境中进行战略性思考？现有研究大多评估LLMs对均衡策略的遵循或其展示的推理深度，但未明确它们是否展现出战略思维，即形成关于其他智能体的连贯推测、根据这些推测评估可能行动并对其做出最佳回应的能力。我们开发了一个框架，通过在系列非合作环境中分离静态完全信息游戏中的信念形成、评估和选择来识别这种能力。通过联合分析模型揭示的选择和推理轨迹，并引入一种新的无上下文游戏以排除从记忆中的模仿，我们表明战略思维是脆弱的。
tldr: 本文通过新框架和上下文无关游戏，揭示了大型语言模型在战略思维上的脆弱性，即它们难以形成连贯推测并据此最佳回应。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals the fragility of strategic thinking in large language models by developing a framework and a context-free game to disentangle belief formation, evaluation, and choice, showing models struggle with coherent conjectures and best responses.
